query: For high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could improve dynamic strength–ductility performance? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an untreated baseline, defines the boundary conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing short-range order (SRO) into high-entropy alloys (HEAs) through appropriate processing techniques can improve their dynamic strength-ductility performance.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with a random solid solution structure
generation.intervention: Introduction of short-range order (SRO) through processing techniques such as severe plastic deformation or annealing
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range order (SRO) in the alloy structure
generation.mechanism: SRO promotes work hardening and enhances ductility by increasing the stacking-fault energies and hardness
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dynamic strength-ductility performance, with increased yield strength and ductility
generation.baseline: HEAs with a random solid solution structure and no SRO
generation.boundary: The improvement in strength-ductility performance is expected to hold for HEAs with a single-phase (disordered) structure and a sufficient amount of SRO
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of SRO required for optimal strength-ductility performance is uncertain and may depend on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of HEAs with varying amounts of SRO
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of SRO does not lead to an improvement in strength-ductility performance, the hypothesis is falsified
